content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a polished, responsive bookmark manager.

Features include:

- Add, edit, archive, restore, and delete bookmarks
- Search with `⌘/Ctrl + K`
- Favorites and tag filtering
- Grid and list views
- Multiple sorting options
- Local browser persistence
- Responsive mobile navigation
- Seeded example content and empty states

Verified with desktop and mobile browser tests; the production build passes without console errors.

[Open Markly](http://maker:4000)

This looks really nice and clean, and I can see it doing most of what I hoped — I can save links, tag them, favorite them, search, switch between grid and list, sort, and archive things I don't want cluttering the list. That all works for me.

One thing is off from what I expected around actually *saving* a bookmark. When I hit "Add bookmark," it asks me to type in the title and the description myself. What I pictured is that I just paste the web address and the app goes and grabs the page's title and description (and the little site icon) for me automatically — that's the main convenience I was after, so I'm not retyping what's already on the page. Right now the icon seems to just be the first letter of the site.

Could you make it so that pasting a link fills in the title and description on its own (I can still tweak them if I want)? Once adding a bookmark works that way, I think this covers what I need.

content:
Updated the bookmark flow:

- Paste a URL to automatically fetch its page title, description, and favicon.
- Fetched text remains fully editable.
- Real site icons appear on saved cards, with the letter icon as a fallback.
- Clear loading, success, and error feedback is shown.
- Private/local URLs are blocked for safety.

Verified end-to-end against live webpages with no console errors.

[Open the updated Markly app](http://maker:4000)

That's exactly what I was after. I pasted a link and it filled in the title and description on its own, pulled the site's real icon, and I could still edit the text before saving — and it sensibly refused a private/local address. Combined with everything else (tags, search, favorites, archive, sorting, the grid/list views, and it all sticking around on my device), this does what I set out to do: save links quickly and manage them without fuss.

I'm happy with it. Thank you.
